title: Biefeld-Brown vacuum tests: 1990 Air Force and 1956 Paris
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Biefeld-Brown vacuum tests: 1990 Air Force and 1956 Paris, about 1956; 1990 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: For example, in 1990, the Air Force tested a Biffield Brown experiment in a vacuum, but they only used 19 kovts instead of the mega voltage Brown was using.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1990 the US Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect, an idea from the inventor Townsend Brown that very high voltage can make a device push itself along, inside a vacuum. According to Michels, the Air Force used only 19 thousand volts, far below the millions of volts Brown used, and he sets this beside an earlier test in Paris in 1956. He tells it to suggest the Air Force test may not have been a fair check of Brown's claim.
